_comment: Hand-written prose that carries judgement. Scalar measured values live in numbers_auto.json and are substituted into these strings by the builder.
SUPP_INTRO: This file contains the regulatory mappings, the executed-scenario record and the sequence diagrams that accompany the main text. Supplementary Table S1 gives the WADA Code articles and the chaincode functions implementing them; Supplementary Table S2 does the same for the GDPR articles; Supplementary Table S3 lists the thirteen regulatory workflows executed end to end against the deployed network and the outcome observed in each. Supplementary Figs S1–S5 trace five of those scenarios as they execute, and Supplementary Fig. S6 shows the transaction-processing sequence of the deployed network. All are reproducible from the archived reference implementation.
RESULTS_STATE_PARA_1: Twelve identical rounds — same workload, same transaction count, same configured send rate — executed back to back against a network brought up clean returned committed throughputs ranging from {{STATE_MIN}} to {{STATE_MAX}} transactions per second (median {{STATE_MEDIAN}}, n = {{STATE_N}}, coefficient of variation {{STATE_CV}}%). The largest and the smallest differ by a factor of {{STATE_RATIO}}. Nothing distinguishes these rounds from one another except when they ran.
RESULTS_STATE_PARA_2: We expected the spread to be explained by the growth of the state database, since the sequence writes {{STATE_TOTAL}} sample records in total and an earlier three-pass execution of the full suite had differed by a factor of {{PHASE1_FACTOR}} in the same direction. It is not. Throughput is uncorrelated with round index (r = {{STATE_R}}), and the last three rounds ({{STATE_LAST3}} transactions per second) match the first three ({{STATE_FIRST3}}). The variation belongs to the single host on which the deployment and its load driver contend, not to the size of the ledger. Its consequence is methodological, and it applies to the earlier version of this work as much as to any other single-round benchmark: one round drawn from this distribution supports no statement about the capacity of the network. Every figure reported below is therefore a range across replicated rounds, and where the difference between two configurations is the quantity of interest it is measured within pairs rather than between separately acquired means.
RESULTS_ENDORSEMENT_PARA: The integrity control on which the framework's response to systematic manipulation depends — endorsement spanning two organisational classes, so that no single organisation can alter committed results — was measured by alternating the two endorsement policies so that the members of each pair are adjacent in time. Across {{PAIRED_N}} pairs the two-organisation policy sustained {{PAIRED_2ORG}} transactions per second against {{PAIRED_1ORG}} for the single-organisation policy, a reduction of {{PAIRED_PCT}}% (range {{PAIRED_PCT_RANGE}}%), in the same direction in every pair. The single-organisation arm itself drifted by {{PAIRED_DRIFT}}% between the first and the last pair, which is the quantity the pairing removes. The absolute rates of this experiment ({{PAIRED_1ORG}} and {{PAIRED_2ORG}} transactions per second) are lower than the corresponding rows of Table 2 ({{ENDORSE_1}} and {{ENDORSE_2}}), and both lie inside the replicate ranges reported there: the workload, the endorsement policies and the configured send rate are identical, and the experiments differ only in when they ran, which is the between-round variation of the preceding section acting on the same operation. The unpaired difference between those two rows of Table 2 is {{ENDORSE_PCT}}%; the paired estimate of {{PAIRED_PCT}}% is the figure of record, and the gap between them is the drift the pairing removes. This corrects the figure of approximately 7% reported in the earlier version of this work, which compared two rounds measured at different moments on a host whose between-round variation exceeds the effect being measured. The cost of the framework's principal integrity control is closer to a tenth of write throughput than to a twentieth, and the spread across pairs shows that even a paired design does not pin it more precisely than that on this deployment.
RESULTS_THROUGHPUT_PARA: Table 2 reports committed throughput and end-to-end latency for every regulated operation, each the mean of {{N_REPLICATES}} replicate rounds with the observed range; Fig. 5 shows the same measurements against configured send rate. {{TOTAL_TX}} transactions executed across the replicated suite with {{TOTAL_FAILED}} failures. Committed write throughput ran from {{WRITE_MIN}} to {{WRITE_MAX}} transactions per second across the six write operations, the slowest being results management, which reads a complete custody chain before it writes. Read-only regulatory evaluation reached {{READ_MAX}} transactions per second: evaluating the decision table requires neither ordering nor commitment, so it is bounded only by the peers' capacity to simulate it. The regulatory logic itself is therefore not the constraint on any of these paths.
RESULTS_LATENCY_PARA: End-to-end latency is dominated by queueing wherever the configured send rate exceeds what the network commits, and at those points it measures queue depth rather than responsiveness. Below saturation, at a configured 10 transactions per second, mean latency was {{SUBSAT_LAT}} for a committed {{SUBSAT_TPS}} transactions per second; at a configured 100 it was {{SAT_LAT}}, and the difference is time spent waiting rather than time spent committing. The floor is the two-second ordering batch timeout configured for this deployment, below which no committed transaction can fall while blocks are not full. Reported latencies should be read with the configured send rate that produced them, which is why Table 2 and Fig. 5 carry both.
RESULTS_RESOURCE_PARA: Container resource accounting sampled at {{RES_INTERVAL}}-second intervals throughout a sustained saturating write round (n = {{RES_N}} samples) locates the cost in state persistence rather than in consensus. The ten CouchDB state databases accounted for {{COUCH_PCT}}% of the processor time consumed by the deployment, {{COUCH_PEER_RATIO}} times the peers themselves at {{PEER_PCT}}%, while the ordering service accounted for {{ORDER_PCT}}%. Aggregate utilisation reached {{HOST_UTIL}}% of the eight available processors, so the ceiling is not processor exhaustion alone. CouchDB is not incidental to the design: the attribute-based access-control model performs rich queries over consent records that the embedded alternative cannot serve. The cost of granular athlete data sovereignty is therefore measurable, and it is borne in state persistence. This is an attribution from resource sampling and not a controlled substitution; no embedded-state-database counterfactual was run, so the magnitude of the penalty attributable to CouchDB specifically is not quantified here.
RESULTS_BASELINE_PARA: To express these figures against something other than themselves, the same custody-initiation write — the sample record and its step-0 custody event, committed atomically and flushed to disk — was executed against a single unreplicated CouchDB instance on the same host, with no endorsement, no ordering, no validation and no second copy of the state. The control sustained {{BASE_TPS}} transactions per second over {{BASE_N}} runs at a mean latency of {{BASE_LAT}} seconds. It too was bounded by its own client concurrency rather than by the database — throughput equalled the achieved send rate throughout — so it is itself a lower bound, and the ratio of at least {{BASE_FACTOR}} to one against the equivalent ledger write understates the difference. That ratio is the price of the governance guarantees: multi-organisation endorsement, ordered commitment, independent validation at every peer, and a tamper-evident record on ten replicas rather than one copy on one node. Mean latency differs by more than two orders of magnitude, {{BASE_LAT}} seconds against the seconds-scale figures of Table 2 — a factor of roughly 140 against the custody-initiation row — of which two seconds is the ordering batch timeout alone. The comparison is deliberately generous to the control and should be read as the order of magnitude of the difference rather than as a benchmark of either system.
RESULTS_DRIVER_PARA: At the higher configured send rates the two co-resident load-driver workers achieved less than the rate they were configured for, which admits two readings: the network refused the offered load, or the driver never offered it. Repeating the two highest sweep points with a six-worker driver, and adding a point at a configured 200 transactions per second, {{DRIVER_VERDICT}} The measurements are reported throughout against configured send rate with the achieved rate shown alongside (Fig. 5a), so that the distinction remains visible to the reader rather than resolved silently.
DISC_MEASUREMENT_PARA: The performance measurements correct this work's earlier claims rather than confirming them, and the correction is as much methodological as numerical. An earlier version projected 300–500 transactions per second for a five-organisation network on analytical grounds and then reported a single measured round of 17.7. Neither figure survives. Twelve identical rounds on this deployment span {{STATE_MIN}} to {{STATE_MAX}} transactions per second, so the reported 17.7 was one draw from a distribution whose spread is larger than most of the differences the paper went on to attribute to design choices — including the 7% endorsement cost, which measured within pairs is {{PAIRED_PCT}}%. The generalisable point is not about this system: a single benchmark round on a shared host is not a measurement of a distributed system, and the practice of reporting one is common enough in this literature that we would expect the same exercise to unsettle other published figures. Where the constraint lies is nevertheless clear and stable across replicates. Resource attribution places it in state persistence rather than consensus, and the state databases responsible are required by the attribute-based access-control model rather than incidental to it, so the cost of granular data sovereignty is real and is paid in storage. The hybrid arrangement of on-chain references and off-chain encrypted payloads is not itself the constraint: such architectures have been shown to sustain adequate performance across multi-organisational configurations while keeping sensitive payloads off the ledger^47^.
DRIVER_VERDICT: raised the load the driver managed to offer without raising what the network committed. At a matched configured rate of 100 transactions per second the six-worker driver offered {{DRIVER_100_SEND}} transactions per second against {{SAT_ACHIEVED}} for two workers, and committed {{DRIVER_100_TPUT}} against {{SAT_TPS_RANGE}}. Offering more load therefore did not raise committed throughput, which is the criterion set out in Methods for the ceiling belonging to the network rather than to the driver. Committed throughput did not merely fail to rise, however: it fell to the bottom of the two-worker range, because the extra workers take processor time from the network they measure — resource sampling puts the driver's own consumption at roughly a tenth of the deployment's load. On a single host the driver cannot be separated from the system under test, so these figures are a lower bound on what the network can commit rather than a measured ceiling.
RESULTS_DEMAND_PARA: Whether this is sufficient for the workload the framework targets depends on parameters that are not published, so we give the calculation rather than a verdict (Methods). WADA reported approximately 330,000 samples analysed globally in 2022^20^. Writing *t* for the ledger transactions a sample generates over its lifetime and *k* for the fraction of the annual total falling in the busiest hour, peak demand is 330,000·*t*·*k*/3,600 transactions per second. At *t* = 30 and *k* = 0.01 — a concentration {{PEAK_FACTOR}} times the mean hourly rate — the reference is {{DEMAND_HIGH}} transactions per second, the figure quoted in the earlier version of this work; at the *t* = 6 that this implementation actually generates for a sample carried through the complete workflow, it is {{DEMAND_LOW}}. Averaged across the year rather than concentrated, the same annual volume is {{DEMAND_MEAN}}. Measured custody-write throughput on this deployment — the median of the {{STATE_N}} identical custody-initiation rounds of Fig. 5c, {{STATE_MEDIAN}} transactions per second with a range of {{STATE_MIN}} to {{STATE_MAX}} — therefore sits above the reference under the implementation's own transaction count and straddles it under the more demanding assumption. Since the measurement is a lower bound and the reference spans an order of magnitude, the defensible statement is that a national-scale testing programme is within reach of a single commodity host and a global one is not demonstrated here.
METHODS_STATE_RESULT: The hypothesis was not supported. Throughput across the twelve rounds is uncorrelated with round index (r = {{STATE_R}}) and the last three rounds match the first three, so accumulated state does not explain the difference between the sequential passes. What the sequence does establish is the between-round variation of this deployment — {{STATE_MIN}} to {{STATE_MAX}} transactions per second, coefficient of variation {{STATE_CV}}% — which is the distribution any single round is one draw from, and which governs how the rest of the measurements are reported.
DISC_LIMITS_OPENING: The deployment ran on a single commodity host with all containers, including the load driver, contending for eight virtual processors; the measurements characterise that deployment and not a provisioned production cluster, and no fifteen-, thirty- or hundred-organisation configuration was measured or extrapolated. Between-round variation on this host is large enough ({{STATE_CV}}% across twelve identical rounds) that differences smaller than roughly a third cannot be resolved except within pairs, which is why the endorsement cost is reported that way and why no other pairwise claim is made.
DISC_DRIVER_CAVEAT: The load driver could not be separated from the system it measures: it consumes roughly a tenth of the deployment's processor load, and increasing its worker count lowered both the offered and the committed rate. Every throughput figure here is therefore a lower bound on network capacity rather than a saturation point, and a driver on separate hardware is a precondition for any claim of a ceiling.
ABSTRACT: Elite athletes' biological data move between clubs, federations, anti-doping organisations and laboratories without standardised governance, and anti-doping records remain centralised and mutable. Blockchain remedies have been proposed but not built. We implemented and evaluated a five-organisation Hyperledger Fabric network, one certification authority per organisational class, executing World Anti-Doping Code Articles 2, 5, 6, 7 and 14 and GDPR Articles 7, 9, 17, 22 and 25 as smart contract logic. Results-management logic is a pure, total function over seven conditions; enumerating its complete 192-vector condition space confirmed determinism and exposed two under-specifications in our earlier decision table: undefined rule precedence and an unhandled laboratory-accreditation state. Thirteen regulatory workflows executed end to end, all passing. Endorsement spanning two organisational classes prevented any single organisation from altering committed results, at a paired cost of {{PAIRED_PCT}}% of write throughput; purpose-limited access released two of six data categories to an authorised researcher, with a recorded reason for each refusal. Twelve identical benchmark rounds varied {{STATE_RATIO}}-fold ({{STATE_MIN}}–{{STATE_MAX}} transactions per second), so any single-round figure is uninterpretable, including one we previously reported; state persistence consumed {{COUCH_PCT}}% of processor time against {{ORDER_PCT}}% for consensus. Formalising regulation as executable code exposes ambiguities that prose conceals.
T2_CAPTION: Committed throughput and end-to-end latency by regulatory operation on the deployed five-organisation network.
T2_NOTE: Each value is the mean of n = {{N_REPLICATES_NUM}} replicate rounds executed against the same deployed network, with the observed range in parentheses; at this n a range is more informative than a standard deviation. The final column is the transaction count of one replicate round. {{TOTAL_TX}} transactions executed in total with {{TOTAL_FAILED}} failures. Latency is end-to-end, from submission to commit notification, and includes the two-second ordering batch timeout configured for this deployment; where the configured send rate exceeds what the network commits it measures queue depth rather than responsiveness. Throughput values are lower bounds rather than saturation points: the load driver is co-resident with the network and consumes {{DRIVER_PCT}}% of its processor load (Methods). Between-round variation on this host is {{STATE_CV}}% (Fig. 5c), which exceeds most of the differences between rows. Measurements were taken on a single commodity host with 8 virtual processors and 11.6 GB of memory available to the container runtime, hosting all 34 running containers including the driver. GDPR, General Data Protection Regulation; WADA, World Anti-Doping Agency.
T3_PERF: Measured: {{N_REPLICATES_NUM}} replicates per round, {{STATE_N}} identical rounds for between-round variation, plus driver-saturation and centralised-writer control arms
F5_TITLE: Measured performance of the deployed five-organisation network.
F5_LEGEND: **a**, Committed throughput and achieved send rate against configured send rate. The two are separated because the driver did not always offer the rate it was configured for; error bars span the range across n = {{N_REPLICATES_NUM}} replicate rounds and markers are their means. **b**, Mean end-to-end latency against configured send rate, same rounds and error bars; latency past the point where offered load exceeds committed throughput is queueing delay. **c**, Committed throughput of {{STATE_N}} identical rounds — same workload, same transaction count, same configured send rate — against the number of sample records already committed, on a network brought up clean. The spread across these rounds is the between-round variation of the deployment ({{STATE_MIN}}–{{STATE_MAX}} transactions per second); it is uncorrelated with accumulated state (r = {{STATE_R}}). **d**, Committed throughput by regulatory operation, means across n = {{N_REPLICATES_NUM}} replicates with the range as error bars; endorsed writes and read-only evaluations are distinguished by colour. All panels: single commodity host, 8 virtual processors, load driver co-resident with the network, so throughput is a lower bound rather than a saturation point.
